patterns.name: Professional Title in Display Name
patterns.description: User includes their company, project, title, or role in their Telegram display name. This is standard practice in crypto, Web3, and tech communities for networking and credibility. Examples: 'Frank | DODO', 'Alex // Keyring Network', 'Sam (Quantstamp)', 'Lore | Tether Gold'.
indicators: Display name contains a company or project name separated by |, //, (), or -
Title like CEO, CTO, Co-founder, Lead, Head of in the name
Name format matches common professional patterns
User is participating in relevant group discussion

patterns.name: Bot Verification / CAPTCHA Message
patterns.description: Automated bot message asking new members to verify themselves by solving a math problem, clicking a button, or completing a CAPTCHA. Common bots: Shieldy, Combot, Rose, ChatKeeperBot, GroupHelpBot. These are anti-spam measures set up by group admins.
indicators: Message from a bot account (name ends in Bot)
Asks to solve arithmetic or puzzle
Mentions being kicked if not verified
Contains a time limit for verification
Powered by a known bot service

patterns.name: Event / Meetup Link Sharing
patterns.description: User sharing a link to an event, meetup, conference, or community gathering via well-known platforms. Links to luma.com, eventbrite.com, meetup.com, lu.ma, etc. are normal community activity.
indicators: Link to known event platform (luma.com, eventbrite.com, meetup.com, lu.ma)
Context is about organizing or attending an event
Shared in a relevant community group
No request for money or personal information

patterns.name: Scheduling Link from Known Contact
patterns.description: A known contact or established group member sharing a Calendly, Cal.com, or other scheduling link for a legitimate meeting. Different from fake reconnection scams because the sender is a known contact or has an established presence.
indicators: Sender is a known contact (is_contact: true)
Sender has been active in shared groups
Scheduling link from known platforms (calendly.com, cal.com)
Context of ongoing professional relationship

patterns.name: Product / Service Discussion with Fees
patterns.description: Users discussing real products, services, or protocols that involve fees, prices, or payments. Mentions of 'pay the fee', 'costs $X', 'deposit required' in context of legitimate product discussion are normal, not scam indicators.
indicators: Discussion about a real, known product or service
Comparison between competing products
Mention of fees in informational context (not asking the reader to pay)
User has relevant bio or expertise
Discussion in a topic-relevant group

patterns.name: Group Welcome / Rules Message
patterns.description: Automated or admin-posted welcome messages for new group members. Often contains group rules, guidelines, or links to resources. May mention restrictions or consequences for rule violations.
indicators: Message welcomes a new member by name
Contains group rules or guidelines
Posted by admin or bot
Mentions group-specific topics or resources

patterns.name: News / Article / Thread Sharing
patterns.description: User sharing links to news articles, blog posts, Twitter/X threads, or research. Links to known media platforms are normal information sharing.
indicators: Link to known media platform (x.com, twitter.com, medium.com, substack.com, mirror.xyz)
User adds brief commentary about the content
Shared in relevant discussion context
No request for action from readers

patterns.name: Legitimate Job Posting
patterns.description: Real job posting from an established company or project. Different from fake job scams: uses known company name, links to official careers page, doesn't require upfront payment, has realistic compensation.
indicators: Posted by or references a known company
Links to official careers page or job board
Realistic job description and compensation
No upfront payment or deposit required
Contact via official channels (email, application form)
